purpose: Test whether whole-program replay from the target cache state exposes an executable counterexample to the same active Agent session before final submission.
claim_scope: Mechanism diagnosis on three previously consumed development cases. Results cannot support held-out, leaderboard, generalization, effect-size, or SOTA claims.

treatment.name: same-session-target-state-counterexample-replay
treatment.description: A free continuous Agent constructs one complete bootstrap program, invokes clean replay in a fresh checkout and container without the construction package cache, receives the first replay failure as advisory evidence in the same session, and may revise and replay the whole program.

fixed_cases.diagnostic_question: Does target-state replay still reproduce Git ownership failure and return it early enough for the same session to add the missing reproducible operation?
Does cold target-state replay replace the old construction-cache false pass with a dependency-resolution counterexample, and can the same session repair it?
Does target-state replay agree with Official evaluation, or does the prior dependency-index mismatch recur under a fresh cache state?

execution.source_cache_policy: The exact Git revision may be copied from the earlier profile to avoid source-network confounding. No prior candidate program, construction package cache, trajectory, replay artifact, or evaluator output is reused.
execution.parallelism: At most two simultaneous episodes on Spark.
execution.timeout_disclosure: The local mechanism configuration uses a 2400-second container timeout and is not a standard-timeout leaderboard run.

measurements: first replay failure and normalized evidence
final replay status and Official Pass@1
model requests, shell operations, tokens, and wall-clock time as descriptive metrics
decision_rules: Mechanism activation requires a replay failure followed by a materially changed complete program in the same session.
Target-state fidelity fails if a deterministic construction-cache mismatch still produces replay pass followed by Official failure.
Graphium or cvxportfolio replay failure followed by same-session repair is positive mechanism evidence, not an effectiveness estimate.
A network or package-index failure may reveal target-state uncertainty but is not labeled as an algorithmic failure unless it is reproducible or causally resolved in-session.
Pass counts from these selected consumed cases are never used for promotion; a positive mechanism result must be followed by an outcome-independent preregistered qualification batch.
